title: Disease and outcome sharing
dependency: Fresh paired summaries and extreme-specialist audit
works: The heatmap, aligned disease forests and support plot already tell the core story in our visual language.
change: Retain the four-panel layout. Give conditional J−O/J−D comparisons a visible place. Keep one disease/domain order across comparable maps. Identify means/CIs separately from descriptive medians/IQRs. Increase legend space beneath B without reducing data area.
acceptance: All plotted models and horizons named, B uses exported paired uncertainty, no unsupported equivalence claim, and unusually large gains are accompanied by absolute specialist AUC and support.

title: Every supervision contrast
dependency: Fresh paired cell tables
works: Exhaustive disease × outcome maps reveal heterogeneity hidden by averages.
change: Keep the original grids. Paginate by clinical domain or use landscape pages at readable type size. Add a labelled OPERA−joint panel as an architectural contrast, keeping it separate from the supervision factorial. Avoid shrinking five maps onto one page.
acceptance: Every intended outcome and disease is present, unsupported cells differ from zero, and signed scales are shared for the same metric.

title: Sharing across prediction horizons
dependency: Fresh horizon-specific estimates and support
works: The original four forest panels are readable and make horizon effects directly comparable.
change: Preserve the design and full negative range. Reserve room for long domain labels and add supported-cell counts in the caption/table. Use a companion common-roster sensitivity rather than interpreting changing task composition as a time effect.
acceptance: All six horizons, interval definitions, model identities and denominators are correct. Layout is acceptable provisionally, not a final-data sign-off.

title: Own correction and borrowing versus training support
dependency: Fresh trained controls, support summaries and mechanism audit
works: The scatter, two coloured support trends and support-band forest communicate partial pooling well.
change: Keep this visual grammar. Remove the precise crossover line/number. Label own−global, full−own and full−global explicitly as separately fitted models. Move the harm-selection scatter to the rescue supplement or name its global-only baseline precisely. The quadratic log-event trend and row-bootstrap ribbon are descriptive.
acceptance: No claim of an event-count threshold, no causal learning curve, no additive AUC decomposition, and caption matches the actual horizon scope.

title: Routed versus joint and adapter controls
dependency: Primary AB control identities and matched rosters
works: Paired domain forests show both helpful and unhelpful effects without decorative emphasis.
change: Keep the forests. Separate primary revised-router controls from the original-router bank sensitivity. Replace aliases with a short descriptive key. Use original-versus-revised as sensitivity, not a second opportunity to pick a winner.
acceptance: Each row identifies architecture, encoder and contrast; crossing zero is not called equivalence.

title: How the gate allocates weight
dependency: Fresh selected-fit route export
works: The disease/outcome bank matrices and allocation bars provide useful structural diagnostics.
change: Keep the matrices and all source columns, including source-only diseases. Make bank-size and flat-allocation references explicit. Label the last panel as entropy of mean weights, not patient-level stability. Do not equate gate mass with useful transfer or the null slot with the unscaled shared path.
acceptance: Rows and columns match the selected checkpoint, bank denominators are correct, own sources are identifiable, and per-patient stability claims use per-patient evidence.

title: Which disease-source corrections matter? Mean replacement
dependency: Fresh source-removal provenance and mean/zero comparison
works: The original square source × target layout is the right idiom for an exhaustive dependence map.
change: Keep it, but use interpretable common units and a fixed shared scale across mean/zero. Display unavailable cells separately. Prefer raw estimates plus uncertainty and a clearly separate shrinkage diagnostic. Remove normalized positive-share or lineage summaries when the underlying effects are near zero.
acceptance: Exact source direction and intervention are labelled. Effects are fixed-fit reliance, not donor training effects. Weak effects remain visually weak.

title: Disease-source effects in detail
dependency: Fresh ablation levels, pair estimates and controls
works: The original forest and domain-map combination permits a detailed audit beyond the overview.
change: Keep the composition but split it over pages if necessary. Give full-source removal, single-source removal and leave-one-in controls distinct names. Do not equate the ablation's none condition with a separately trained own-only fit. Use the same map scale as the overview.
acceptance: Baselines, retained global/outcome paths, pair denominators and mean replacement references are explicit.

title: Disease-source dependence: zero-replacement sensitivity
dependency: Fresh zero exports and same target roster as mean
works: A matched map makes the sensitivity transparent.
change: Retain the same order, scale and units as mean replacement. State that zero removal changes the average offset as well as individual variation. Avoid presenting this as independent replication.
acceptance: Matched mean/zero provenance, no automatic colour amplification and no claim that the two interventions are interchangeable.

title: Zero-replacement details
dependency: Fresh zero-export detail tables
works: The original detailed view supports diagnosis of source effects.
change: Match the mean-detail layout and baseline key. Keep uncertainty readable. If duplicating the entire page adds little, retain the estimates as a table plus a compact mean-versus-zero comparison.
acceptance: The sensitivity remains available even if its full duplicate plate is moved to the archive.

title: Overall performance and consolidation
dependency: Fresh primary/national roster, clinical protocol and subgroup tables
works: The old reference ladder, per-cell comparison and horizon panels are more informative than the LDH simplification.
change: Keep the familiar arrangement. Make the primary model explicit in every panel. Include the relevant model families and encoder variants in a compact absolute-performance panel, with the full list in the companion overview. Avoid mixing joint and OPERA under one identity. Move duplicate clinical/subgroup panels out if they crowd the central comparison.
acceptance: No stale clinical panel, no missing panels disguised as results, both tabular strategies retained, and no national winner selected on test performance.

title: All declared models on a common roster
dependency: Final model roster and common supported cells
works: The point distributions and model summaries show the portfolio honestly.
change: Keep the original horizontal structure. Group primary models, encoder variants and sensitivity controls with whitespace. Use identical cell rosters for directly compared summaries and explain when points describe tasks rather than patients.
acceptance: All declared variants are visible, descriptive means are not labelled bootstrap intervals, and changing availability is reported.

title: Comparison with strong tabular predictors
dependency: Fresh X/XP/neural reconciliation
works: Domain forests, the event-support scatter and horizon profiles are useful and stylistically established.
change: Keep the four panels. Spell out the baseline for every gain, use the same clinical-domain taxonomy as pooling and leave a dedicated legend band below D. Show pooled XGBoost as well as per-task XGBoost. Retain negative neural differences.
acceptance: Common risk sets/metrics verified, full x ranges visible, no unexplained groupings, and the support trend is not described as an experiment varying training size.

title: Discrimination and conventional calibration
dependency: Fresh calibration and prespecified example cells
works: The old domain forests and reliability examples connect ranking with probability quality.
change: Retain this style. Use full reliability curves with counts and uncertainty rather than examples represented by one bin. Choose examples by a rule fixed before test. Avoid duplicating the headline and tabular plates in full.
acceptance: Raw calibration, readable examples, clear AUC versus slope interval definitions, and no example chosen for an attractive held-out result.

title: Calibration across models and clinical domains
dependency: Fresh raw slopes/intercepts and reliability curves
works: The original slope/bias forests are an important counterweight to AUC-only reporting.
change: Keep conventional plots. Preserve finite extremes, using a labelled expanded view or explicit compressed scale rather than clipping. Show estimation failures and cell counts. Replace any one-point reliability example with a supported prespecified example. Do not silently recalibrate the reported model.
acceptance: Ideal slope 1 and zero bias clear, all finite intervals retained, and IQRs are not called CIs.

title: Absolute predictability
dependency: Declared model identity and fresh atlas
works: The support scatter and domain summaries provide context for the size of gains.
change: Keep the original two panels. Explicitly label the fixed joint reference or add a separately named OPERA companion. This is absolute performance, not evidence that sharing caused improvement.
acceptance: Model and aggregation named, zero/support exclusions accounted for, and task variation distinguished from uncertainty.

title: Every disease and outcome: absolute AUC
dependency: Fresh atlas and coverage mask
works: An exhaustive matrix is valuable and should remain available.
change: Preserve all cells and make grey unavailable distinct from below-chance AUC. Paginate into readable landscape domain blocks, with repeatable legends and support alongside. Do not reduce type to fit one page.
acceptance: All 69 endpoints and declared diseases covered, final-size labels legible and exclusions traceable to coverage.

title: Which disease–outcome questions can be estimated?
dependency: Fresh fit/support reasons
works: The categorical grid reveals what a headline average leaves out.
change: Keep the full matrix and counts. Distinguish too few training events, missing exports, one-class evaluation and confirmed fitting failures. Do not label absent specialist predictions as failed fits without a receipt.
acceptance: Legend totals reconcile, states are mutually interpretable and this comparison's roster is not confused with the model's ability to predict.

title: Training-event scarcity across the whole grid
dependency: Full training-support export including zeros
works: The full grid and cumulative distribution directly motivate sharing.
change: Keep the original all-cell view rather than cropping to supported cells. Explicitly display zero, unknown and inapplicable counts. Annotate evaluation support separately from descriptive training-event bands.
acceptance: Full denominators retained and the five-case/control criterion is not misrepresented as a training-event threshold or proof of clinical precision.

title: Corrections in tasks where joint sharing was harmful
dependency: Frozen tuning-defined strata evaluated on held-out data
works: The original scatter and small forest communicate the heterogeneity better than a complex redesign.
change: Keep that layout. Name the x/y baselines and the tuning-defined strata. Mark tuning-on-tuning results descriptive. On test, retain the original tuning strata rather than redefine hurt cells using test outcomes.
acceptance: No circular claim of rescue, paired estimates retain the same tasks and supported denominators are shown.

title: One shared model versus a selected portfolio
dependency: BEST_TUNING predictions and a declared selection roster
works: The old scatter/selection-bar layout makes consolidation concrete.
change: Keep it. Reserve more space for A and align the legends. Include OPERA in an expanded selection policy only as a separately named, development-frozen strategy. Do not compare selection frequencies for one roster with performance of another without labelling it.
acceptance: The previously missing performance panel is populated by selected-model predictions, selection uses tuning only, and all models share the reported evaluation population.

title: National pretraining and cohort adaptation
dependency: National downstream models and actual fraction runs
works: The original three-origin comparison and label-efficiency panels fit the sharing argument.
change: Keep this design. Separate joint and OPERA within each encoder origin, show paired national−local and adaptation increments, and use observed training fractions. Avoid interpolated sample-saving claims without uncertainty and a declared rule.
acceptance: No national values filled from synthetic previews, all six planned arms accounted for, matched cells and actual training fractions identified.

title: Where national information helps
dependency: National subgroup contrasts and coverage
works: A compact forest is appropriate for prespecified heterogeneity.
change: Keep the original forest style and support/coverage strata. Report all declared subgroups with uncertainty, not only beneficial ones. Do not confuse fewer vocabulary matches with fewer clinical events.
acceptance: No empty placeholder presented as a null result, no post-test subgroup search and no inference of national benefit before downstream evaluation.

title: Patient-subgroup performance
dependency: Fresh patient-level subgroup aggregates
works: Paired forests keep the subgroup story clinically readable.
change: Keep the old forest arrangement. Group rows by covariate with whitespace, include subgroup denominators and show uncertainty. Use one declared primary identity and do not conflate patient strata with task-level training-support bands.
acceptance: Every subgroup uses documented matching/weighting and missing subgroup data remain visible.

title: Geographic heterogeneity within Denmark
dependency: Fresh region aggregates, geometry and missing-region counts
works: The map plus quantitative intervals balances geographical orientation and effect size.
change: Keep it. Increase vertical space before the lower row and retain full x ranges in every forest. Use consistent model colours in all panels and separate colourbars for different quantities. The maps are within-system heterogeneity, not independent geographic validation.
acceptance: Region denominators and missingness reconcile, lower labels do not clip, and legend meanings do not change unnoticed across panels.

title: Patient representation and predicted risks
dependency: Fresh selected-fit coordinates, risks and projection provenance
works: The old seven-panel map is visually engaging, with the same patients recoloured for different questions.
change: Keep this style and shared bounds. For A, retain a faint pooled cloud with a small number of directly labelled centroids/contours, plus full disease facets as a companion. Do not use 24 competing contours as the only disease key. Separate predicted-risk points from estimated calibration surfaces.
acceptance: Every disease is identifiable somewhere, map stage and projection fit are recorded, and geometry is not interpreted as proof of predictive benefit.

title: Every disease on the same patient map
dependency: Fresh coordinates and fine-disease membership
works: Highlight-one-disease facets solve the crowded map's identification problem.
change: Keep all fine diseases on identical coordinates and bounds, with readable n labels. Paginate if necessary. Keep the background faint but visible and do not refit a separate projection in each facet.
acceptance: Every observed disease appears, no point omission and no pooled category silently substitutes for fine diseases.

title: Status, predicted risk and local calibration on the embedding
dependency: Fresh selected-fit predictions, status, vectors and residual estimates
works: The original repeated-outcome grid allows direct visual alignment.
change: Retain the grid but give each row a short, readable label. Split arrows into their dedicated plate. Use common residual limits that include all finite values or visibly flag saturation. Distinguish smoothed observed risk from patient predicted risk.
acceptance: No clipped values without markers, masks/support explicit, unchanged projection across rows, and conventional calibration reported separately.

title: Projected corrections across outcomes
dependency: Raw-vector audit and fresh shared-coordinate vector exports
works: A dedicated arrow row is much clearer than arrows buried in a five-row plate.
change: Keep the current pre-LDH arrow style, common magnification and status key. Add a short numerical similarity summary in the caption. Similar arrows cannot identify the global adapter or establish useful routing.
acceptance: Base/adapted vectors use one fixed projection, raw-vector agreement reviewed, and no claim that an arrow points towards risk.

title: Representations across encoder/readout stages
dependency: Matched-stage coordinates, patient identities and projection recipes
works: A stage-by-covariate atlas is useful as a descriptive supplement.
change: Retain small multiples and common style. Show observed category membership rather than an averaged ordinal clinical score. State when stage projections are separately fitted. Separate encoder representations from outcome-specific routed readouts.
acceptance: No displacement claim between independent projections, stage identities complete, and final routed risk may vary without moving the shared encoder map.

title: Recorded information associated with each predicted risk
dependency: Corrected IG, code labels, references and concept support
works: The original source/time bars beside the outcome–concept matrix contain substantial auditable information.
change: Keep the visual language. Split into clinical-domain pages with repeated legends and readable labels. Show expected-direction boxes only where an actual documented expectation exists. Unmapped concepts stay explicitly unresolved. Explain signed covariance shares and reference dependence without calling them causal variance explained.
acceptance: All Danish labels auditable, counts and unsupported concepts visible, no unsupported biological sign claims, and no tiny one-page atlas masquerading as readable print artwork.

title: Outcome similarity and information-removal effects
dependency: Fresh IG agreement and restricted-input results
works: The original similarity matrix and removal comparison are both strong diagnostic ideas.
change: Keep both, but split onto separate pages if labels remain small. Label what agreement statistic is used. Treat nested endpoint definitions as a source of expected similarity. Add uncertainty for restrictions or point to the complete paired-effect table.
acceptance: Attribution agreement is not positive transfer; removal at evaluation is not retraining without that source; the pooled-outcome estimand is explicit.

title: Overview of model-input dependence
dependency: Fresh IG/restrictions plus explicit synthetic-episode labels
works: The original multi-panel overview links sources, concepts and a timeline.
change: Keep it as an optional summary rather than another main figure. Avoid repeating the full atlas and structure plots. The recipe currently points to synthetic_patient_episodes_risk.csv: the patient timeline is a synthetic illustration, not a newly explained clinical patient.
acceptance: Synthetic panel labelled individually, concept units explicit, all empirical panels use the same audited checkpoint and no unlabelled mixture of illustration and results.

title: Illustrative patient history and multiple risks

change: Retain only if it teaches something the atlas cannot. The recipe uses synthetic_patient_episodes_logodds.csv. Label it Synthetic patient prominently and name the logit/risk scale; do not imply an actual patient-level IG export or sensitivity result.
acceptance: Figure and caption both identify the illustration, all events respect the treatment landmark, and the bubble magnitude legend names the quantity.

acceptance: No synthetic values, horizon and pooled-across-disease estimand explicit, same patients/checkpoint and last-week boundaries verified.
